claims.text: Increasing the Ir fraction by approximately 10% relative to equiatomic PtPdRhRuIrOs will enhance durability during ethanol oxidation.
Ir enrichment will suppress deleterious surface oxide formation.
The suppression of surface oxide formation is caused by an Ir-induced modification of local electronic structure.
The initial catalyst is an equiatomic nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
Increasing Ir while reducing a more oxophilic component will alter the catalyst surface composition.
The altered surface composition will adjust the catalyst electronic structure.
The electronic-structure adjustment will reduce the binding energy of oxygenated intermediates.
Ir sites are more resistant to oxidation under the stated ethanol-oxidation conditions.
A higher proportion of Ir sites decreases the tendency to form strongly bound surface oxides.
Weakening adsorption of oxygenated species mitigates catalyst deactivation.
The Ir-enriched catalyst will exhibit lower surface oxide coverage than the equiatomic baseline under identical electrochemical conditions.
The Ir-enriched catalyst will retain a more stable catalytic current over prolonged potential cycling than the equiatomic baseline.
The hypothesized relationship applies under moderate temperatures, controlled electrolyte environments, potential cycling, and composition changes around 10% relative to the equiatomic state.
A statistically significant failure to reduce oxide formation and improve current stability relative to the equiatomic control would falsify the hypothesis.
